title: Pentecostalism worldwide
hook: from a plain mission on Azusa Street to Pentecostal churches across Africa, Asia and Latin America

segments.voice: Yesterday: millstone, a wound inside the house, and the millstone Jesus spoke of. Your line: believe them.

No stained glass. No steeple. No pews. On Azusa Street in Los Angeles, a plain wooden building, once used as a stable and a storeroom, has sawdust on the floor and planks laid across barrels for benches. At the front stands a preacher named William Seymour, the son of formerly enslaved parents, with a pair of wooden crates for a pulpit. In the room, Black and white and Latino worshipers, washerwomen and businessmen, side by side, in a city and a country that kept them apart. People pray out loud, weep, sing, and some speak in tongues.

Pentecostalism takes its name from Pentecost, the day in Acts when the Holy Spirit comes on Jesus's followers in Jerusalem. In the King James Bible: "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." Then Peter stands up and quotes the prophet Joel: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy." Pentecostals read that as a promise for now, not only for then. Speaking in tongues, prophecy, prayer for healing: the gifts of the Spirit, they say, are for ordinary believers today. And it showed in who led. At Azusa Street, women preached, and Black and white Christians laid hands on one another, which shocked plenty of observers. One early participant wrote, in effect, that the color line had been washed away. It didn't stay washed; Pentecostal churches later split along racial lines too, and that's part of the story. Some historians say the movement didn't spread from one center like spokes from a hub. They point to revivals with similar marks around the same era in India, Korea, Chile and parts of Africa, many led by local preachers rather than visiting missionaries. Today Pentecostal and charismatic churches are found from Lagos to Seoul to São Paulo, and charismatic renewal has reached Catholic and older Protestant churches too. Christians differ here. Pentecostals say the gifts continue. Some other Christians hold that certain gifts, like tongues, belonged to the apostles' time. Both read the same chapter of Acts.

Bring to mind a Pentecostal or charismatic church you've passed: a rented room above a shop, a big hall by the highway, a congregation meeting in a school gym on Sundays. Picture the people walking in, the music starting, someone raising their hands, and let yourself be curious rather than wary. If you pray, pray for that congregation.
Pentecostalism worldwide. A movement that reads Pentecost as a promise for today, with gifts of the Spirit for ordinary believers, now found across Africa, Asia and Latin America.
Your line: the spirit on all flesh. Sons and daughters alike. Nine hundred seventy-five days now.

howItsDone: Pentecostal worship is often loud and expressive, with long sung praise, raised hands, spontaneous prayer, prayer for healing, and speaking in tongues. Charismatic groups in Catholic and other churches pray in similar ways within their own traditions.

chat.says: Did every Pentecostal church grow out of that one revival on Azusa Street?
options: Some historians say no: similar revivals sprang up then in India, Korea, Chile and Africa, often led by locals.
Yes, every Pentecostal church today was started by missionaries sent out from that one room.
No, the movement began in Seoul and reached Los Angeles only many years later.
chat.meaning: Some historians say Pentecostalism had many centers, not one hub: revivals with similar marks rose around the same era in India, Korea, Chile and Africa.

Azusa Street.meaning: the Los Angeles street where the revival met

William Seymour.meaning: the preacher who led the Azusa Street meetings

speak in tongues.meaning: to pray aloud in unknown languages, which Pentecostals see as a gift

Joel.meaning: a Hebrew prophet whom Peter quotes at Pentecost

charismatic.meaning: stressing the Spirit's gifts, within many kinds of churches

notes: Claims rule: the index's 'hundreds of millions today' is left out; no counts or dates. 'Found from Lagos to Seoul to São Paulo' is a non-numeric description.
Azusa Street mission details (former stable/storeroom, sawdust, planks on barrels, wooden crates as pulpit): commonly reported; confirm.
Seymour as the son of formerly enslaved parents: confirm.
'One early participant wrote, in effect, that the color line had been washed away' paraphrases Frank Bartleman ('the color line was washed away in the blood'); confirm attribution.
Later racial splits among Pentecostals: confirm general wording.
Independent revivals in India (e.g. the Mukti revival), Korea, Chile and Africa 'around the same era': confirm or soften.
Cessationist view described as 'some other Christians hold that certain gifts... belonged to the apostles' time'; confirm fair and unranked.
The screen head 'PENTECOST: TONGUES OF FIRE' draws on Acts 2:3 (cloven tongues like as of fire); the voice quotes 2:4. Confirm acceptable.
